findings.note: Before this programme every authority in the repository existed only as a prose table or an article of an instrument. The tier lattice alone was machine-readable. Consequently no gate could resolve which authority was competent for an act, no gate could detect an authority referenced but never defined, and no gate could detect that a recorded claim of authority absence had been contradicted by later located evidence. Closed by deriving the registry from the located instruments rather than by authoring a second authority model.
findings.title: The authority model was prose-only, so no gate could resolve a competence question

findings.note: The meta-constitutional projection records a vacant constitutional tier on the evidence that no ratified normative artifact occupies it. Located instruments elsewhere record an exogenous constituent act that identified the sovereign seat, chartered a standing ratification organ, and fixed document supremacy. Both are Repository Truth. Deciding between them is reserved to the claim owner under CEP-002 Article 23; this programme measures both sides, cites both, and refers. It does not promote any instrument into the vacant tier, which CMG-000001 XVII.4 forbids and LXXXI.5 voids.
findings.title: A recorded vacancy and later located evidence of authority both stand; the conflict is referred, not decided

findings.note: This programme can prove from located evidence which authority is competent for an act. It cannot perform the act: CEP-006 I.5 provides that ratification authority is never self-conferred by execution authority and acts only upon an authorization, and CEP-006 I.4 caps any in-corpus determination at PROVISIONAL. Recording a ratification is therefore owned by the ratification registry, and conferring one is owned by the located authority — never by this engine.
findings.title: Competence to ratify and the ratifying act are distinct, and only the first is closable by measurement

findings.note: The runtime refused an authorization that 'asserts a foreign authority', but no gate could say which authorities were not foreign: the minted token was a free string bound to no registered authority, to no vesting instrument and to no tier. Nothing prevented a module from minting a token that reads as a constitutional authority, and nothing required a new authority-shaped constant to be disclosed. Closed by DISCOVERING every such token from the executable plane and measuring two independent properties — that no token collides with a registered constitutional authority, and that every discovered token is classified with its basis. The declared classes cannot narrow the discovered population and cannot waive the collision check.
findings.title: The executable plane minted authority tokens that resolved to nothing

findings.note: CMG-000001 ARTICLE XVI.2 legislates the one precedence lattice as prose and CMG-REGISTRY.json projects it as data; every gate that resolves rank reads the projection. Acyclicity and vacancy completeness were validated, but membership, tier name and located status were never compared against the canonical instrument, so a projection could drift from what it projects and every dependent gate would inherit the drift silently. The charter's own four-tier vesting, which XVI.5 obliges the lattice to remain consistent with, was likewise unmeasured. Closed by reading all three located instruments against each other. Corroboration is computed only for tiers the projection already reports located, so no measurement here can promote an instrument into the recorded vacancy.
findings.title: The tier projection every gate reads was never read against the instrument it projects
